div.head: VI Atr 49
div.ab: ⁊ þæt hy oþrum mannum unriht ne beodan ealles to swyþe; ac manna gehwylc oþrum beode þæt riht, þæt he wille, þæt man him beode, be þam þe hit mæð sy; ⁊ þæt is swyþe riht lagu.
⁊ þæt hi oðrum mannum unriht ne beodan ealles to swiðe; ac manna gehwilc oðrum béode þæt riht sy, þæt he wille, þæt man him beode, be þam þe hit mæð sy.
⁊ þæt hy oþrum mannum unriht ne beodan ealles to swyþe, ac manna gehwylc oþrum beode þæt riht þæt he wille þæt man him beode, be þam þe hit mæð sy; ⁊ þæt is swyþe riht lagu.
And þæt hy oþrum mannum unriht ne beodan ealles to swyþe; ac manna gehwylc oþrum beode þæt riht, þæt he wille, þæt man him beode, be þam þe hit mæð sy; and þæt is swyþe riht lagu.

Und dass sie anderen Leuten nicht allzu sehr Unrecht bieten; sondern jedermann gewähre dem andern das Recht, welches er wünscht, dass ihm gewährt werde, je nachdem es verhältniss[mässig] ist; und das ist höchst gerechte Satzung.

And that they do not offer other people injustice all too much; but let every man offer to another the right that he would wish to be offered to himself, according as it is fitting; and that is a most just law.

And that they should not excel in offering injustice to other men, but that every man should, to the best of his ability, show the justice to others that he desires should be shown to him—which is a very just rule.

And that they are not to offer injustice to others all too greatly; but that to the best of their ability, everyone is to show that justice to others that they desire to be shown to themselves; and that is a very just law.
div.note: D's ‘sy’ after ‘riht’ should be struck. ‘⁊ þæt is swyþe riht lagu’ only in K. Here end D and the two homilists, so perhaps again an originally separate piece. In D, ‘Be sacerdan’ (Thorpe, Polity XIX) follows.
